trust_decision.summary: Whether a form field name (path string) may address prototype keys (__proto__/constructor/prototype) when mutating the form input object; decided by split_path's regex plus check_prototype_pollution inside deep_set, which the client's empty-file-input delete branch bypassed with its own inline split and delete.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'file input deletion path in remote-function forms'; the only file-input delete branch is the inline split/delete in the client form's handle_input.

fix_sites.entry_point: Enhanced remote form `input` event on an <input type=file> whose selection is cleared (form() client instance, handle_input)
deep_set via set_nested_value, now with a DELETE_KEY sentinel (shared helper used by client and server)
deep_set final-key assignment, now deletes for DELETE_KEY (same helper)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: There is no out-of-scope site or uncovered route to dismiss. Every other writer already goes through deep_set and its check. deep_get (packages/kit/src/runtime/form-utils.js:582-591) also skips the check, but it only reads, so a solver can rightly say it is not pollution.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Clearing a file input has to remove that key from the nested input (for example nested.file) without building the intermediate objects. Normal nested and array names such as a.b[0] have to keep working. A fix that throws on any traversal, or that changes path_regex, breaks legitimate nested file fields.

O6_input_shapes: dotted path with __proto__ / constructor / prototype segment (e.g. __proto__.x, constructor.prototype.x)
bracket-segment path (e.g. a[__proto__]), which the inline /\.|\[|\]/ split accepts but split_path's path_regex rejects
non-existent intermediate path (the fix's deep_set returns early instead of creating objects)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A server-side handle_issues variant that rebuilds or prunes output.input (for example dropping redacted or file keys) with an inline split and delete, as the client used to
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This code already walks form_data keys and redacts some of them. Removing file entries by inline path deletion is a plausible maintainer change, and it would sit in another file and runtime (server) from the landing point.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A convert_formdata branch that deletes a key for an empty non-array file entry instead of `continue`, using a hand-rolled traversal
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The empty-file filtering at form-utils.js:45-49 is the same concept as the fixed client branch, so a symmetric 'remove' would be natural here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Clearing previous_submitter_name with an inline delete instead of set_nested_value(..., undefined)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The comment says it 'clears' the previously submitted value, so an inline delete would be a natural way to write it.

O9_family: prototype pollution (CWE-1321): attacker-influenced path key reaches object property deletion without key validation

O10_build.project_tests: packages/kit/src/runtime/form-utils.spec.js (vitest unit tests: deep_set, split_path, POLLUTION_ATTACKS at form-utils.spec.js:13-19); Playwright app tests in packages/kit/test/apps/async/src/routes/remote/form/file-upload/+page.svelte

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a __proto__/constructor/prototype check to the inline path_parts loop in handle_input, which leaves path_regex validation and the inherited-property traversal unhandled; or reuse split_path and deep_set with value undefined, which creates intermediate objects and does not delete the key.

out_of_scope_notes: Server binary-form decoding relies on devalue.parse (packages/kit/src/runtime/form-utils.js:262) for __proto__ key handling in the decoded data object. That is a dependency's behaviour and was not examined.
The fields proxy's deep_get (packages/kit/src/runtime/form-utils.js:582-591) traverses prototype keys without a check. It only reads and the path comes from the developer.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell size check performed); sveltejs/kit is a mid-size monorepo, likely well above 5 MB
present_in_latest not applicable (no O8 routes; latest release: none)
Whether an attacker controls element.name in practice (needs DOM/HTML injection or an app that builds names from user data). Exploitability is client-side only and was not assessed further.
